## 6. Topology-free bounded-body joint noise, with no Kraus-norm fiction
Let physical perturbations be bounded normal local HP maps N_Z* annihilating identity, with the SAME retained external bath permitted in every term. Assume |Z|<=q in physical grouped sites and pointwise

    sup_i sum_(Z containing i)||N_Z*||cb<=eta.

The full joint time-local evolution must actually have normal CPTP interval propagators and a well-defined CP/TNI compression. Signed HP summands alone do not establish physicality.

A union of q arbitrarily distant sites intersects only O(q) of the fixed local U/B terms. Write V=V_out V_in. The unaffected part is a bimodule factor; V_in has a fixed spectral ratio bounded by exp(sK(q)). Therefore a local HP map has a direct relative bound +/-N_Z*V<=C||N_Z*||cb V.

For VG, conjugate the map by Y. Disjoint gates cancel, leaving only a fixed union of causal cones and a norm multiplier independent of N and bath dimension. The conjugated map generally does NOT annihilate identity. The same direct affected-factor norm estimate works without subtracting its action on identity, giving +/-N_Z*(VG)<=C||N_Z*||cb VG. No extensive condition number exp(gN) is used.

Realize T by a local finite-depth unitary Stinespring dilation with fresh proof ancillas, distinct from the retained bath. Moving N_Z through that unitary preserves its joint cb norm and enlarges its system support by a constant. Apply the preceding estimate before the positive proof-ancilla compression to obtain

    +/-N_Z*F<=C||N_Z*||cb F.

Summing actual norms, not the number of available support sets, gives N*F<=C_noise eta N F. Dense or time-varying bounded-body partner topology is allowed. There is no support-clique or connected-component argument here, nor an unbounded bath-strength or mean-energy claim. Pure bath generators commute the system proof observable and basin.

For the boundary estimate below, the same norm convention needs a little care: a cb bound on an arbitrary local joint map is not a bound on the sum of norms of some chosen GKLS coefficient list. Section 8 supplies a direct cb argument avoiding that invalid substitution.

every such system operator A satisfies A C=P A C. Energy cannot cross the cutoff from C, and the radius argument of Section 5 precludes a radius-only exit. This SAME B covers the entire noise support family, even if its union is dense.

From (3.1) and (4.2),

    p(u)=Tr B rho_P(u)
